text:
Maya: FYI we have a support escalation from AcmeMaps — they're getting a lot of 429s on /v1/generate since 11:02 UTC and observed intermittent high p99 latency. I can repro locally with their API key.

Maya: repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME-XXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1","input":"test burst"}'
```

Priya: they reported a ramp during a UI rollout — could be quota exhaustion or client retry storm. Customer says they were under their monthly quota though.

Kevin: grabbing limiter logs for that org id (acme_org_42). Throwing the latest redis sample here — looks suspicious:

```
LIMITER:org:acme_org_42 tokens=0 refill_rate=0.000000 burst_window=1 last_refill=1678901234 ttl=0
LIMITER:org:acme_org_42 tokens=0 refill_rate=0.000000 burst_window=1 last_refill=1678901290 ttl=0
```

Kevin: refill_rate=0 and ttl=0 — that explains tokens not replenishing. I think the Redis TTL never got set due to a codepath that returns early on a specific error.

Maya: hmm. We saw a spike in ingress to the dedicated pool for this tenant at 11:01 which lines up. But if refill isn't running, bursts would be permanently drained and they'd 429 even under reasonable sustained load.

Kevin: digging into limiter service code (limiter v1.2.7). Found two issues:
1) env var typo in our per-tenant override loader: we look up BURST_WINDOW_SEC but ops configured BURST_WINDOW_SECS — fallback to default 1s.
2) Redis setex call for token buckets used ttl_seconds variable that can be 0 on certain code paths when rate == 0 (bug introduced in commit abc1234). That results in keys created with no expiry, and another codepath that expects to touch TTL returns early, leaving refill timers disabled.

Kevin: minimal repro on staging: create bucket with refill=0 (simulate bug) then call refill loop -> tokens stay 0.

Maya: We need an emergency mitigation for impacted tenants while we push a fix. Options: temporarily lift burst enforcement for acme_org_42 via feature flag, or increase global burst window. Prefer per-tenant change.

Priya: Customer asks for ETA and mitigation. I recommended we enable temporary exception for them to stop 429s and let them finish rollout.

Maya: I'm applying a temporary rule via the config service to set burst_window=60s for acme_org_42 and to bypass token check for up to 200 rps for 10 minutes. Pasting CLI step I ran: 
```bash
redwoodctl config set --org acme_org_42 limiter.override.burst_window=60 --ttl 600
```

deploy-bot: @Maya initiated feature-flag change limiter.override.burst_window for org=acme_org_42 -> ttl=600s (change id ff-20260315-07).

Kevin: I'll prepare a hotfix to restore correct TTL behavior and make env-var parsing robust. Plan: patch limiter library to always set positive TTL (default 24h) and accept both BURST_WINDOW_SEC and BURST_WINDOW_SECS. Also add unit & integration tests. Target PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/limiter/pulls/128 (wip) commit patch id abc1234 -> fix -> def5678 (will replace).

Maya: Rolling canary of limiter-fix to prod now (limiter v1.2.8-canary).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: limiter v1.2.8-canary -> 3 instances in us-west-2. Healthchecks passed.

sre-oncall: Monitoring: 429s for acme_org_42 dropped from 18% -> 0.5% within 90s of the feature flag. p99 latency back to baseline.

Kevin: Hotfix merged to main (commit def5678), CI green. Going to schedule full rollout with a progressive percentage increase and an automated rollback if errors spike > 1%.

deploy-bot: Production rollout: limiter v1.2.8 -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (no rollback triggered).

Priya: AcmeMaps confirmed resolved on their side and appreciated the fast response.

Tom: Nice work. We should add a customer-facing summary and update the incident tracker.

Maya: Opening an incident ticket and adding notes. Action items for postmortem:
- Patch permanent fix & release (done)
- Update limiter runbook with explicit env var names and expected TTL semantics
- Add canary verification that TTL > 0 for new limiter keys
- Create alert: Monitor fraction of limiter keys with ttl==0 across shards (threshold 0.1%)
- Add test simulating per-tenant override with plural/singular env vars

Kevin: I'll take the runbook + tests. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Priya: I'll send the customer summary and close the support ticket after Tom reviews.

Maya: Marking this thread as resolved for now. Follow-up: postmortem doc link (draft) https://go.redwood.ai/postmortems/limiter-20260315-draft — will ping when final. :white_check_mark:

Tom: thumbs up :+1:

Maya: closing.
